articles.title: You Don't Need a Current-Gen Console if You're Happy to Play GTA 6 at Xbox Series S Settings
articles.summary: After months of speculation, Rockstar finally revealed that GTA 6 would be targeting 30 fps on all of the current-generation consoles, including the Xbox Series S. But, thanks to a cloud streaming deal with Xbox, you can technically play the game on the Xbox One.
body: While GTA 6 will only be running locally on the PS5 and Xbox Series consoles, Rockstar finally detailed which devices will be able to use Xbox Cloud Gaming to play the game. Its blog post says, "The game will also be available via Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One consoles, utilizing Xbox Series S graphics settings." So, you can technically play GTA 6 on the Xbox One, which launched all the way back in 2013, it just won't be, well, running on the Xbox One itself.

We've known for a while that GTA 6 would be playable via Xbox Cloud Gaming, after an exclusive deal was announced in October. At the time, because of the wide swath of devices that can use Xbox Cloud Gaming, this deal fueled speculation that you'd be able to play GTA 6 on everything from a gaming PC to an iPhone. However, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball later clarified that the game wouldn't be streaming to PC. But, now, thanks to Rockstar's blog, we now know the full extent of devices that can stream GTA 6.

articles.title: Here’s How Your Xbox One Can Play GTA 6
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is out next week, and the game is launching on both Xbox Series X|S and PS5. If you don't have an expensive current-generation system, it previously appeared you would be out of luck to play GTA 6, but that's not the case.
body: Rockstar officially confirmed on November 10 that Grand Theft Auto 6 will support Xbox Cloud Gaming. This feature allows you to stream the game to Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One, and uses Xbox Series S graphics settings. This means it'll look a little worse than running it natively on the Xbox Series X, but if you are still rocking with an Xbox One, this is the only way you can play the game.
"And as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay," Rockstar added in its announcement.

The catch to all this is that Microsoft just so happened to add a time limit to Xbox Cloud Gaming starting in November. If you have a Game Pass Ultimate subscription, you can play 15 hours a month via Xbox Cloud Gaming. Those without a subscription can buy time, as well, but 50 hours will cost $12, and that's on top of the cost of Grand Theft Auto 6 itself.
points: Grand Theft Auto 6 is out next week, and the game is launching on both Xbox Series X|S and PS5.
If you don't have an expensive current-generation system, it previously appeared you would be out of luck to play GTA 6, but that's not the case.

articles.title: GTA 6 PS5 Pro Features, Frame Rates, And Xbox Cloud Gaming Details Confirmed By Rockstar
articles.summary: Rockstar has finally shared details on what PlayStation 5 Pro owners can expect from Grand Theft Auto 6 on their expensive consoles, but has also confirmed that all platforms will run at the exact same frame rate.
body: PlayStation 5 Pro players can look forward to PSSR support, which will use Sony's well-tuned upscaler to provide a cleaner image compared to that on the base PS5. Additionally, ray-traced shadows will be exclusive to the PS5 Pro version, which might make a noticeable difference across Leonida depending on the time of day.

All of this will run at 30 frames per second across all platforms, Rockstar confirmed, with no mention of additional performance modes. Recent datamines suggested that GTA 6 might have numerous performance modes and additional frame rate support, but that doesn't seem to be the case yet.

In addition to PS5 Pro support, Rockstar has also announced that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming at launch. This means you won't need an Xbox Series X|S or PlayStation 5 to play arguably the biggest game of the year, with the Xbox One also supported via streaming exclusively. Cloud streaming won't be available on PlayStation consoles, but remote play (streaming from a console in your home) is supported on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Big Walk’s AI Usage Was Tiny, But Its Disclosure Has Sparked A Bigger Debate
articles.summary: Big Walk developer House House has confirmed that it used AI during the "final stretch" of its development. The studio recently updated its FAQs page to confirm its use of the tech, with the news coming after 19 Independent Games Festival jurors announced they'll decline to vote for "any game that…
body: There's a lot to unpack here, starting with why House House didn't disclose the use of AI for Big Walk. The game is hosted on platforms like Steam, where studios can voluntarily disclose AI usage when it comes to generated code (however, it is mandatory to disclose if a game has AI-generated assets), but House House says it only did so after the topic became a matter of public interest. It also added that it will continue to support developers looking to limit "the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world."

Pathologic 2 localization writer Bruno Diaz also touched on the controversy, explaining that IGF rules required studios to disclose the use of AI in development. Game designer Austin Walker posted online that the IGF committee has been debating the use of AI in game development, leading 19 jurors to issue a statement. While the group says it doesn't speak for the entire IGF organization or all jurors involved in the IGF Awards, IGF leadership supports the statement. Overall, if AI is used in any part of a game's development, from coding to visual assets, the jurors will not vote for it.

articles.title: Nintendo’s New Gift-Giving Feature Comes With Some Very Nintendo Restrictions
articles.summary: A new update is available for all Nintendo Switch 2 and Switch consoles, and if you're on a Nintendo Account family plan, version 23.5.0 will allow you to once again gift games to members in your group.
body: "Just in time for the holidays, a new feature will let family group members gift digital games to other members of their group," Nintendo wrote in an update. "You will be able to gift digital products that you purchase through Nintendo eShop on your device to family group members. This includes eligible games as well as DLC and upgrade packs."

In typical Nintendo fashion, what should be a straightforward program does have some strange restrictions. The company has noted that not every item is eligible for digital gifting and that the number of digital gifts handed out within a specific period is limited. This isn't the first time that Nintendo has offered a digital gifting program, as way back in the Wii era, owners of the console could visit the Wii Shop and grab some WiiWare or Virtual Console games. From there, users were free to gift them to anyone on their Wii friend list. That service was eventually closed after the Wii Shop Channel was shut down in 2019.

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Run at 30fps On All Consoles, Features Ray Tracing Improvements on PS5 Pro
articles.summary: Rockstar has finally announced performance for GTA 6. It’ll run at 30fps on all consoles, but PS5 Pro enhancements improve ray tracing. “Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30…
body: That means no matter what console you play on — PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, or Xbox Series S — the game will run at, or below, 30fps. “Targeting 30fps” is different to locked 30fps, so there’s likely some fluctuation in busy scenes.

Ray tracing allows for finer detail in shadows, as well as shadows that naturally blur and widen the farther away they get from the object casting them, matching the physical size of the light source. Improvements here are only available on PS5 Pro.

There are also some PlayStation exclusive details in the controls, which support high-fidelity haptic feedback on the DualSense controller — Rockstar says it “fully integrated” this into the game. The same goes for Sony’s Tempest 3D audio for spatial sound improvements.
Those last two are true for both base PS5 and PS5 Pro. All this and improved load times make “Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles,” according to Rockstar.

articles.title: How to get the Scarecrow Song in Ocarina of Time
articles.summary: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, the Scarecrow Song is an optional but useful song you can unlock to help you get to otherwise impossible to reach places. You don't need the song to beat the game, but you will need it to get every Piece of Heart and Skulltula Token.
body: The song allows you to summon a scarecrow to a set location, allowing you to use your Hookshot to jump over to it. Nifty!
Below, we explain how to unlock the Scarecrow Song in the Ocarina of Time remake.

As young Link, talk to the scarecrows at Lake Hylia. They're right at the entrance on the farmed land. Pierre, the one closer to the entrance of the lake, will tell you to come up with a song yourself using your ocarina. Note that whatever you play here will become the Scarecrow Song. Feel free to be creative, but keep in mind that every time you play the Scarecrow Song, you'll have to watch Link play it out as you play it here. This means if you drag the song out to be very long, you'll get a long cutscene each time.

Memorize whatever you play here, take a screenshot of it, or write it down, as the game will not record it anywhere for you (yet). Talk to Bonooru, the second scarecrow, and play the song for him. He'll love it!
points: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, the Scarecrow Song is an optional but useful song you can unlock to help you get to otherwise impossible to reach places.
You don't need the song to beat the game, but you will need it to get every Piece of Heart and Skulltula Token.

articles.title: BoJack Horseman: A Top Animated Season in TV History
articles.summary: Occasionally, a TV show will come out that sticks with viewers even after they have finished watching it. Some seasons are even powerful enough to "enter the cultural zeitgeist as some of the best seasons.
body: Those are, of course, all live-action television shows that have achieved that status. It's rare for an animated series to be able to join those shows, but one Netflix series managed to do that.

BoJack Horseman follows BoJack Horseman (Will Arnett), a washed-up former television star living in Los Angeles. He's a man clothed in misery and contempt, and each season sees him burrowing further into his self-destructive behavior while pushing away everybody around him, from roommate Todd Chavez (Aaron Paul) to Princess Carolyn (Amy Sedaris).

By season four, BoJack Horseman had hit its stride. The characters were all developed and central enough to begin exploring more about their pasts, and after a devastating season three finale, it was clear that they still had a lot more to offer. As season four began, and BoJack escapes California, it is far from the new beginning or the true escape that he hoped for.

body: Rockstar shared the news in a blog post released to announce that GTA 6 pre-loading is now available ahead of its release date on 19th November.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles," Rockstar says. It goes on to reconfirm GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on all consoles, saying the game is pushing modern machines "to their absolute limits" in order to "bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

PS5 players can expect high-fidelity haptic feedback through the DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio, and Tempest 3D audio, while PS5 Pro enhancements come in the form of PSSR support and ray tracing shadows, which should make the game look especially fancy, plus improved load times. articles.title: Nintendo Is Officially Investing in Game Preservation
articles.summary: Game preservation has always been one of the biggest problems facing the industry. According to the Video Game History Foundation, 87% of classic video games released in the United States are critically endangered or lost.
body: A new job posting from Nintendo of America indicates that the company is now looking for a digital archivist. The person hired for the role will "design and implement a structured framework for organizing technical records, engineering documentation, source materials, and institutional knowledge related to legacy systems and platforms." Nintendo says the archivist will help ensure the company's historical records are "preserved for future generations." The position will be on a 12-month contract.

In the past, Nintendo has drawn criticism from the preservation community. In 2022, the Video Game History Foundation publicly criticized the company for announcing it would be closing the Wii U and 3DS eShops. The foundation released a statement saying that Nintendo's decision was "actively destructive to video game history." The statement also pointed out that Nintendo is part of the Entertainment Software Association, which funds lobbying that prevents a number of preservation efforts.

articles.title: Bandai Namco Shuts Down Once-promising Studio after Colossal Failure
articles.summary: Bandai Namco Entertainment, which published 2026 hits like Ace Combat 8 and The Blood of Dawnwalker, is shutting down one of its studios. Bandai announced on Tuesday that it is dissolving Reflector Entertainment, a studio it acquired in 2020 and had high hopes for beyond just its single game…
body: Reflector only developed one game, 2024's Unknown 9: Awakening, a supernatural stealth game that stars The Witcher 's Anya Chalotra. It largely flew under the radar and received a very mixed response from critics; it has a 59 Metascore on Metacritic. Unknown 9: Awakening is part of Reflector's larger Unknown 9 multimedia franchise, which includes a novel, comic book series, and narrative podcast series.

"After comprehensively considering future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation, [Bandai Namco] has decided to discontinue Reflector’s business, dissolve and liquidate it," a news release states. Bandai claimed Reflector will lose €21 million (approximately $23.49 million) in the third quarter of its current fiscal year.

articles.title: Europe is about to get very tough on loot boxes in games, according to a leaked draft of the landmark Digital Fairness Act
articles.summary: An alleged draft of the potentially game-changing Digital Fairness Act has leaked ahead of its scheduled publication tomorrow (11th November), containing proposals that could dramatically affect the way games operate and are monetised within the European Union.
body: The draft, published by French publication Contexte (via Video Games Industry Memo ) goes as far as to recommend that loot boxes (uncertainty-based rewards) be turned off by default for minors, as well as the sale of in-game items and currencies. There's also a recommendation that all players - not just minors - should be able to turn off offers related to these lootboxes and gambling mechanics.

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences," the draft of the Digital Fairness Act begins. "It has enabled faster, more convenient and wider access to an ever-increasing range of goods and services. At the same time, it has given rise to new and more sophisticated ways of influencing consumers' choices.

"Along with the indisputable benefits in choice and efficiency, the extensive use of digital technologies allows both old and new unfair commercial practices to affect consumers at scale, exacerbating risks to their economic interests, as well as to their mental and physical wellbeing. Vulnerable consumers are particularly affected."

articles.title: Rockstar kills any hopes of streaming GTA 6 from Xbox to PC, but you can stream it to your old Xbox One if you like
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S. And as part of the same announcement, the developer revealed a key detail about the game's cloud streaming options.
body: GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming. However, this is only possible on Xbox Series X/S consoles, as well as - surprisingly - the last generation console, Xbox One. Notably, that means you can't use Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream to PC, or other devices, despite it being useable there.

You may recall that in early October, a Verge report said Microsoft had acquired exclusive cloud streaming rights for GTA 6, with the understanding being that the game would be available to stream on any XCloud-supported device - as in, to PC as well. Xbox immediately shot down the report, saying GTA 6 "will not be streaming exclusively or to PC".

Perhaps more surprisingly, the cloud-streamed version will be using Series S graphics settings, not those of the more powerful Series X console. Considering the loss in quality inherent in cloud streaming, this will make for a less-than-ideal way of experiencing the game.
Beyond cloud streaming, GTA 6 supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox, so you can stream the game on your local network to any device, from a PS5 or Xbox Series X/S console.
points: Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S.
GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming.

body: A packed Direct this week as the panel discuss the pros and cons of DLSS for Nintendo first party games like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Meanwhile, HDR experts aren't too impressed by Nintendo's HDR implementations, Rich takes time to test out the Xbox FSR demo on PC and God of War Laufey gets a three month delay. And looking back in time, the panel has praise for EA's 30th anniversary game package, it's 20 years since the launch of Nvidia's 8800 GTX and a decade since John posted his epic Tomb Raider DF Retro episode. And finally, hilarity as Rich discovers how old Oliver was when Tomb Raider first released...
